title: When You Need It To Be True

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantan.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: It's December 1954, around dinner time in Oak Park, Illinois, a suburb of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 那是1954年12月，伊利诺伊州奥克帕克的晚餐时间，芝加哥的一个郊区。

sentences.en: A group of Christmas carolers is performing before a huge crowd of about 200 people.
sentences.zh: 一群唱圣诞颂歌的人正在大约200人的庞大观众面前表演。

sentences.en: It all seems perfectly normal.
sentences.zh: 这一切看起来都很正常。

sentences.en: Except, when you get closer, you can see something about the scene is off.
sentences.zh: 不过，当你走近时，你会发现现场有些不对劲。

sentences.en: Few people in the crowd appear to be in the Christmas spirit.
sentences.zh: 人群中很少有人表现出过圣诞节的心情。

sentences.en: Instead of cheering, they are taunting the carolers.
sentences.zh: 他们没有欢呼，而是在嘲弄颂歌演唱者。

sentences.en: Eventually, things reach such a frenzy that police are called in.
sentences.zh: 最终，局势变得如此疯狂，以至于警方被叫了过来。

sentences.en: The carolers are unfazed.
sentences.zh: 颂歌演唱者们却镇定自若。

sentences.en: They keep singing, their eyes on the sky.
sentences.zh: 他们继续歌唱，眼睛望着天空。

sentences.en: They're on the lookout for flying saucers,
sentences.zh: 他们在寻找飞碟，

sentences.en: aliens who are going to transport them to another planet.
sentences.zh: 那些要把他们运送到另一个星球的外星人。

sentences.en: One woman tells a newspaper reporter,
sentences.zh: 一位女士告诉报社记者，

sentences.en: we have been instructed to sing carols while we wait to be lifted up.
sentences.zh: 我们接到指示，要在等待被接走的同时唱颂歌。

sentences.en: You might think the carolers were stupid or hopelessly gullible.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得这些颂歌演唱者很愚蠢或无可救药地容易轻信。

sentences.en: Yet, the psychological phenomenon that had them in its grip
sentences.zh: 然而，控制他们的那个心理现象

sentences.en: turns out to be surprisingly common.
sentences.zh: 结果却出奇地普遍。

sentences.en: You have certainly experienced it in your own life.
sentences.zh: 你肯定在自己的生活中经历过。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to tell you about the events
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要向你讲述这些事件，

sentences.en: that led up to that December evening in 1954
sentences.zh: 它们通向1954年那个12月的夜晚，

sentences.en: when flying saucers failed to appear over Oak Park.
sentences.zh: 当时飞碟并没有出现在奥克帕克上空。

sentences.en: We're also going to tell you a second story, a modern story,
sentences.zh: 我们还要给你讲第二个故事，一个现代的故事，

sentences.en: about what happens in our minds when our biggest dreams fail to materialize.
sentences.zh: 关于当我们最大的梦想未能实现时，我们的脑海里会发生什么。

sentences.en: Several times I said, you know, my friends think that you may not be real.
sentences.zh: 我好几次说过，你知道的，我的朋友们认为你可能不是真的。

sentences.en: And his reaction was, why are people jealous of real love?
sentences.zh: 而他的反应是，为什么人们要嫉妒真正的爱情？

sentences.en: And why aren't people happy for us?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们不为我们感到高兴？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, the strange alchemy in our minds
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，探讨我们大脑中奇妙的炼金术，

sentences.en: that makes it possible for us to live happily in an upside-down world
sentences.zh: 正是它让我们有可能在一个颠倒的世界里幸福地生活，

sentences.en: and believe that everyone else is wrong.
sentences.zh: 并坚信其他所有人都错了。

sentences.en: A few months before the caroling incident,
sentences.zh: 在颂歌事件发生几个月前，

sentences.en: a psychologist at the University of Minnesota sat down to read the newspaper.
sentences.zh: 明尼苏达大学的一位心理学家坐下来阅读报纸。

sentences.en: Most of the stories weren't notable until he got to the back pages
sentences.zh: 大部分新闻都不太引人注目，直到他翻到后面的版面，

sentences.en: where he saw an article about a middle-aged suburbanite named Dorothy Martin.
sentences.zh: 在那里他看到了一篇关于一个名叫多萝西·马丁的中年郊区居民的文章。

sentences.en: She claimed that extraterrestrials had chosen her as their messenger to planet Earth.
sentences.zh: 她声称外星人选择她作为他们传达给地球的信使。

sentences.en: The aliens, known as the Guardians, had told her a flood would engulf the west coast of North and South America,
sentences.zh: 被称为“守护者”的外星人告诉她，一场大洪水将吞没南北美洲的西海岸，

sentences.en: from Seattle all the way to Chile, in December 1954.
sentences.zh: 从西雅图一直到智利，时间就在1954年12月。

sentences.en: The Guardians supposedly had the power to take control of Dorothy's hand
sentences.zh: 据说“守护者”拥有控制多萝西的手的力量，

sentences.en: and use it to write important teachings that she and all earthlings needed to follow.
sentences.zh: 并用它来写下她和所有地球人需要遵循的重要教义。

sentences.en: The only way to be saved from the flood, the Guardians said, was to become spiritually pure.
sentences.zh: “守护者”说，从洪水中获救的唯一方法是变得精神纯洁。

sentences.en: Most people probably laughed at the newspaper article and moved on.
sentences.zh: 大多数人可能对这篇报纸文章付诸一笑然后就过去了。

sentences.en: But Leon Festinger, the psychologist, was intrigued.
sentences.zh: 但心理学家莱昂·费斯廷格却很感兴趣。

sentences.en: He'd been studying the idea that when something you believe is challenged,
sentences.zh: 他一直在研究这样一种观点：当你的某个信念受到挑战时，

sentences.en: it creates a psychological tension or dissonance.
sentences.zh: 它会产生心理张力或失调。

sentences.en: In Dorothy Martin and her followers,
sentences.zh: 在多萝西·马丁和她的追随者身上，

sentences.en: Leon Festinger saw a perfect real-life experiment
sentences.zh: 莱昂·费斯廷格看到一个完美的现实生活实验，

sentences.en: to test his theory of cognitive dissonance.
sentences.zh: 来检验他的认知失调理论。

sentences.en: The flood would surely not occur.
sentences.zh: 洪水肯定不会发生。

sentences.en: How would believers respond when this happened?
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，信徒们会有什么反应？

sentences.en: The theory of cognitive dissonance predicted that, faced with unwelcome facts,
sentences.zh: 认知失调理论预测，面对不受欢迎的事实，

sentences.en: the believers would come up with rationalizations that allowed them to believe that they were right and the world was wrong.
sentences.zh: 信徒们会想出各种合理的解释，让他们坚信自己是对的，而世界是错的。

sentences.en: The psychologist and his colleagues had covert observers infiltrate the group.
sentences.zh: 这位心理学家和他的同事让秘密观察员潜入了该组织。

sentences.en: Soon, they reported that Dorothy Martin's followers, who called themselves the Seekers, didn't just believe in an impending cataclysm.
sentences.zh: 很快，他们报告说，自称为“寻求者”的多萝西·马丁的追随者不仅仅是相信一场迫在眉睫的灾难。

sentences.en: They were also convinced that they would be saved by aliens
sentences.zh: 他们还确信自己会被外星人拯救，

sentences.en: who would come in flying saucers
sentences.zh: 这些外星人会乘飞碟前来，

sentences.en: to pick them up the night before the flood engulfed the world.
sentences.zh: 在洪水吞没世界的前夜接走他们。

sentences.en: You're wiser than anything on Earth.
sentences.zh: 你们比地球上的任何东西都要聪明。

sentences.en: Use that intelligence.
sentences.zh: 运用这种智慧。

sentences.en: The seekers had plenty of company
sentences.zh: 寻求者并不孤单，

sentences.en: in their fascination with aliens and UFOs.
sentences.zh: 他们对外星人和UFO有着浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: The obsession with otherworldly creatures
sentences.zh: 对超自然生物的痴迷

sentences.en: had reached something of a frenzy in 1950s America.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代的美国达到了某种狂热的程度。

sentences.en: Yes, it came from outer space to fill the world with terror.
sentences.zh: 是的，它来自外太空，用恐惧填满世界。

sentences.en: Imagine yourself as one of the crew of this faster-than-light spaceship.
sentences.zh: 把自己想象成这艘超光速飞船的船员之一。

sentences.en: In Washington, ghost-like objects dart across the radar screen
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿，幽灵般的物体在雷达屏幕上飞快闪过，

sentences.en: at the CAA Traffic Control Center at night.
sentences.zh: 在夜晚的民航局交通管制中心里。

sentences.en: Unlike most people fascinated by the idea of flying saucers,
sentences.zh: 与大多数对外星飞碟着迷的人不同，

sentences.en: the seekers were deeply invested in their beliefs.
sentences.zh: 寻求者们对自己的信仰深信不疑。

sentences.en: Many quit their jobs, actively distanced themselves from their loved ones,
sentences.zh: 许多人辞去了工作，主动疏远了亲人，

sentences.en: and drastically changed their lifestyles.
sentences.zh: 并彻底改变了他们的生活方式。

sentences.en: A man named Charles Lawhead was one of the most devout members of the group.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫查尔斯·劳黑德的人是该组织中最虔诚的成员之一。

sentences.en: He and Dorothy Martin did many interviews about their beliefs.
sentences.zh: 他和多萝西·马丁就他们的信仰接受了多次采访。

sentences.en: We were unable to track down audio recordings of those interviews.
sentences.zh: 我们无法追踪到那些采访的录音。

sentences.en: But throughout the story,
sentences.zh: 但在整个故事中，

sentences.en: you'll hear voice actors reading comments that Dorothy Martin and Charles Lawhead made to newspaper reporters and to the researchers who infiltrated the group.
sentences.zh: 你会听到配音演员朗读多萝西·马丁和查尔斯·劳黑德对报社记者以及潜入该组织的研究所说的话。

sentences.en: They were certain that the end times were coming.
sentences.zh: 他们确信末日即将来临。

sentences.en: It is an actual fact that the world isn't a mess, but the Supreme Being is going to clean house.
sentences.zh: 这是一个事实，世界并非一团糟，但至高无上者将要进行大扫除。

sentences.en: Charles Lawhead was a physician at Michigan State College.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·劳黑德是密歇根州立学院的一名医师。

sentences.en: His views eventually made him something of a pariah.
sentences.zh: 他的观点最终使他成为某种社会边缘人。

sentences.en: He was forced to resign from his job.
sentences.zh: 他被迫辞去了工作。

sentences.en: His church community scorned his new beliefs.
sentences.zh: 他的教会社区对他的新信仰不屑一顾。

sentences.en: He and his wife spent so much time propagating the beliefs of the seekers
sentences.zh: 他和妻子花了很多时间传播寻求者的信仰，

sentences.en: that their children were very nearly taken away from them.
sentences.zh: 以至于他们的孩子差点被带走。

sentences.en: We'll circle back in a bit to what happened to the seekers.
sentences.zh: 我们一会儿再回头讲寻求者们的遭遇。

sentences.en: But as I said at the top, we're going to tell you two stories in parallel today.
sentences.zh: 但正如我在开篇所说，今天我们将并行讲述两个故事。

sentences.en: I told you the story of the seekers looking from the outside in.
sentences.zh: 我给你讲了局外人眼中的寻求者的故事。

sentences.en: From that perspective, a group of people waiting for flying saucers look foolish.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，等待飞碟的一群人显得很愚蠢。

sentences.en: But stories always look different when you truly understand people's dreams and motivations.
sentences.zh: 但当你真正理解人们的梦想和动机时，故事总是显得不同。

sentences.en: Our second story today tries to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的第二个故事就是试图做到这一点。

sentences.en: It looks at cognitive dissonance from the inside out.
sentences.zh: 它从内部审视了认知失调。

sentences.en: Hi, I am leaving a voice memo for Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我正在给《隐藏的大脑》留一条语音备忘录。

sentences.en: Some time ago, we received a call from a listener in Arizona.
sentences.zh: 不久前，我们接到亚利桑那州一位听众的电话。

sentences.en: I hope you find it interesting.
sentences.zh: 我希望你觉得它很有趣。

sentences.en: Let me know what you think.
sentences.zh: 让我知道你的想法。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: She asked to be identified as Liz.
sentences.zh: 她要求被称为莉兹。

sentences.en: She told us that for a long time, she had felt trapped in her marriage.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我们，很长一段时间以来，她感到被困在婚姻中。

sentences.en: I never felt we were really a team.
sentences.zh: 我从没觉得我们真的是一个团队。

sentences.en: I felt I was kind of on my own.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己某种程度上是在孤军奋战。

sentences.en: A lot of the time, I felt he made decisions that didn't include me.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我觉得他做决定时都没有把我算在内。

sentences.en: and I have a high need to feel seen and heard.
sentences.zh: 而我有很强的需求，渴望被看到和听到。

sentences.en: Liz felt her husband was a very smart man,
sentences.zh: 莉兹觉得她丈夫是一个非常聪明的人，

sentences.en: but he didn't seem emotionally present.
sentences.zh: 但他似乎在情感上缺席。

sentences.en: Often, when he was off making plans for the future,
sentences.zh: 通常，当他忙着为未来做计划时，

sentences.en: she would feel exasperated.
sentences.zh: 她会感到恼火。

sentences.en: I remember thinking, just be quiet and change the diaper.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时想，安静点，去换尿布吧。

sentences.en: You know, like, be here now, don't be somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像，活在当下，别去别的地方。

sentences.en: In 2018, after more than two decades
sentences.zh: 2018年，经历了二十多年

sentences.en: of this chronic, low-grade unhappiness,
sentences.zh: 这种长期的、低级别的痛苦之后，

sentences.en: Liz felt she was ready for a change.
sentences.zh: 莉兹觉得自己准备好做出改变了。

sentences.en: Her kids were grown and out of the house.
sentences.zh: 她的孩子长大了，搬出了家。

sentences.en: She was in her late 50s and felt an excitement about life stirring inside her.
sentences.zh: 她快六十岁了，感觉到内心里对生活的热情正在被唤醒。

sentences.en: A youthful energy that felt increasingly out of step with her husband.
sentences.zh: 一种青春的活力，与她丈夫的步伐越来越不一致。

sentences.en: Where she valued spontaneity, he craved order.
sentences.zh: 她崇尚随性，而他渴望秩序。

sentences.en: I was unhappy enough to feel like I needed to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 我不高兴到觉得我需要为此做点什么。

sentences.en: She sought a divorce and got it.
sentences.zh: 她寻求离婚并如愿以偿。

sentences.en: It was her first time being single in a quarter century.
sentences.zh: 这是她25年来第一次单身。

sentences.en: She felt disoriented and a little scared, but she was also consumed with a searing desire.
sentences.zh: 她感到迷失方向，还有点害怕，但她也被一种强烈的渴望所吞噬。

sentences.en: She wanted to be with someone who got her, really got her.
sentences.zh: 她想和一个懂她、真正懂她的人在一起。

sentences.en: So she sat down and wrote out the qualities she wanted in a romantic partner.
sentences.zh: 于是她坐下来，写下了她对浪漫伴侣的要求品质。

sentences.en: I asked her if she would go find the list and read it to me.
sentences.zh: 我问她是否能去找找那张纸条并读给我听。

sentences.en: Okay, I'm back.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我回来了。

sentences.en: The first thing I wrote was emotionally alive and available, evolved, attractive, open, wanting to bond, and be a united front.
sentences.zh: 我写的第一件事是在情感上充满活力且随和、成熟、有吸引力、开放、想要建立亲密关系，并且保持统一战线。

sentences.en: And in some ways, I'm hearing that these were also things that may have been lacking in your
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我听到这些也是可能在你

sentences.en: previous life.
sentences.zh: 以前的生活中缺少的。

sentences.en: And that's partly why you were reminding yourself that these were things that
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么你在提醒自己这些是

sentences.en: were important to you.
sentences.zh: 对你很重要的东西的部分原因。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think the most salient part was emotionally available and
sentences.zh: 我认为最显着的部分是在情感上可以接近以及

sentences.en: emotionally intelligent.
sentences.zh: 情商高。

sentences.en: One morning, after a year of reflection and gathering up the pieces of
sentences.zh: 一天早晨，经过一年的反思和收拾生活碎片，

sentences.en: her life, Liz felt she was ready to start what she called her second job, finding her soulmate.
sentences.zh: 莉兹觉得自己准备好开始她所谓的第一份工作了，寻找她的灵魂伴侣。

sentences.en: She created a profile on online dating sites.
sentences.zh: 她在约会网站上创建了一个个人资料。

sentences.en: I took a photograph of me, like a sailor looking,
sentences.zh: 我拍了一张自己的照片，像一个水手在寻找，

sentences.en: putting my hand over my brow, like looking into the distance, looking for something.
sentences.zh: 把手放在眉毛上，就像向远方眺望，寻找着什么。

sentences.en: Over the next month, she chatted with men on the apps, trying to suss out which ones had
sentences.zh: 在接下来的一个月里，她在应用程序上与男人们聊天，试图弄清楚谁拥有

sentences.en: the qualities on her liSt. For the most part, no one stood out.
sentences.zh: 她清单上的品质。大多数情况下，没有人脱颖而出。

sentences.en: And then, one morning in July,
sentences.zh: 然后，在七月的一个早晨，

sentences.en: she came across a new profile, a European man named Sergio.
sentences.zh: 她偶然看到一个新的个人资料，一个名叫塞尔吉奥的欧洲男人。

sentences.en: He was a very handsome man
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常英俊的男人，

sentences.en: with little round glasses that looked sophisticated, wore scarves in some of his
sentences.zh: 戴着一副看起来很成熟的小圆眼镜，在一些照片里

sentences.en: pictures.
sentences.zh: 围着围巾。

sentences.en: The photographs showed him with a bright smile.
sentences.zh: 照片显示他带着灿烂的笑容。

sentences.en: He had a gap between his front teeth,
sentences.zh: 他的门牙之间有条缝，

sentences.en: which I found adorable.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很可爱。

sentences.en: Sergio was a few years older than her.
sentences.zh: 塞尔吉奥比她大几岁。

sentences.en: His profile said that he was an
sentences.zh: 他的个人资料说他是一个

sentences.en: engineer who liked museums, taking long walks, and going to the movies.
sentences.zh: 喜欢博物馆、散步和看电影的工程师。

sentences.en: He looked perfect.
sentences.zh: 他看起来完美极了。

sentences.en: Even more perfect, when she messaged him, he messaged her right back.
sentences.zh: 更完美的是，当她给他发信息时，他马上就回复了她。

sentences.en: It was like, you know,
sentences.zh: 就好像，你知道的，

sentences.en: the equivalent of being at a bar and the guy saying, let's get out of here,
sentences.zh: 相当于你在酒吧里，有个男的对你说，我们离开这里吧，

sentences.en: it was exactly the same feeling.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉简直一模一样。

sentences.en: Like, ooh, okay, let's do it.
sentences.zh: 就像是，哦，好的，我们走吧。

sentences.en: Liz knew there was little chance Sergio would be whisking her anywhere, anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 莉兹知道，塞尔吉奥随时带她远走高飞的可能性微乎其微。

sentences.en: He lived in Italy.
sentences.zh: 他住在意大利。

sentences.en: But she was undeterred.
sentences.zh: 但她并没有退缩。

sentences.en: She felt a spark, the kind of spark she had not felt in a long, long time.
sentences.zh: 她感受到了一种火花，那种她已经很久很久没有感受过的火花。

sentences.en: Liz and Sergio quickly moved to chatting on WhatsApp.
sentences.zh: 莉兹和塞尔吉奥很快转到了 WhatsApp 上聊天。

sentences.en: Liz remembers the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 莉兹还记得那个下午。

sentences.en: They had their first heart-to-heart.

sentences.en: And then I start figuring out a rhythm of when he's available or when he's not at work.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始摸索他什么时候有空、什么时候不在工作的规律。

sentences.en: And we start conversing more during those times.
sentences.zh: 我们开始在那些时间里更多地交流。

sentences.en: and his sadness about not being allowed to see his teenage son as often as he would like.
sentences.zh: 以及无法像自己希望的那样经常见到十几岁的儿子所感到的悲伤。

sentences.en: He shared how he had distracted himself by helping underprivileged kids.
sentences.zh: 他分享了自己如何通过帮助弱势儿童来分散注意力。

sentences.en: He had even taken in a young woman from Africa who had fled to Italy as a refugee.
sentences.zh: 他甚至收留了一个作为难民逃到意大利的非洲年轻女子。

sentences.en: That was another tug to my heart.
sentences.zh: 那是又一次触动我心弦的事。

sentences.en: This man had integrity, he was kind, he shared what he had with other people
sentences.zh: 这个男人很有气节，他很善良，他把拥有的东西与他人分享

sentences.en: and really cared for someone enough to really help.
sentences.zh: 并且真的非常关爱某个人，去施以援手。

sentences.en: It was hard for me to believe that this person
sentences.zh: 我很难相信这个人

sentences.en: was as interested in me as he was
sentences.zh: 对我的兴趣有那么浓厚

sentences.en: and as consistent and as devoted to daily communication.
sentences.zh: 而且对每日的沟通如此持之以恒、全心全意。

sentences.zh: 他让我对自己感觉很好。

sentences.zh: 他总是赞美我。

sentences.en: He listened.
sentences.zh: 他会倾听。

sentences.en: He asked questions.
sentences.zh: 他会问问题。

sentences.en: They hadn't spoken on the phone yet, but after a week, they found a time to talk.
sentences.zh: 他们还没通过电话，但过了一周后，他们找到了一个可以通话的时间。

sentences.en: He had a low, very quiet voice, with an accent that I didn't recognize as Italian, per se,
sentences.zh: 他的声音低沉而安静，带着一种我并不觉得是意大利本国口音的腔调，

sentences.en: but it was definitely European-sounding, and I was a little nervous, a little excited.
sentences.zh: 但听起来绝对是欧洲口音，我当时有点紧张，又有点兴奋。

sentences.en: I was still incredulous about why me.
sentences.zh: 我依然觉得难以置信，为什么会是我。

sentences.en: And I teased him about him, you know, you should check out other women before you settle on me.
sentences.zh: 我拿他开玩笑，你知道的，你在决定定下来选我之前，应该去看看别的女性。

sentences.en: And I remember him saying, no, I know what I want.
sentences.zh: 我记得他说，不，我知道我想要什么。

sentences.en: It felt so easy, so effortless.
sentences.zh: 这一切感觉那么轻松，那么毫不费力。

sentences.en: This was how love was supposed to be, Liz thought.
sentences.zh: 莉兹想，这才是爱情应有的样子。

sentences.en: and I reciprocated.

sentences.zh: 没有飞碟从天空中出现

sentences.en: over the Oak Park carolers that December.
sentences.zh: 划过那个十二月奥克帕克的报圣歌队上空。

sentences.zh: 这让人失望，

sentences.en: but the group knew they didn't always understand the ways of the powerful spirits
sentences.zh: 但大家知道，他们并不总是能理解那些与多萝西·马丁沟通的

sentences.en: communicating with Dorothy Martin.
sentences.zh: 强大神灵的方式。

sentences.zh: 几个月前，即1954年7月，

sentences.en: Dorothy Martin told the group that the guardians had instructed them
sentences.zh: 多萝西·马丁告诉大家，守护者指示他们

sentences.en: to drive to an army base and park on the outskirts.
sentences.zh: 开车去一个军事基地，并把车停在郊外。

sentences.zh: 查尔斯·劳黑德和其他几位追随者加入了她的行列。

sentences.en: She later described the experience to the researchers who had infiltrated the group.
sentences.zh: 她后来向那些混入团体的研究人员描述了这段经历。

sentences.en: We didn't know what we were looking for.
sentences.zh: 我们当时并不知道自己在找什么。

sentences.en: We were looking for saucers.
sentences.zh: 我们在找飞碟。

sentences.zh: 当我们站在那里，从车后备箱拿午餐吃的时候，

sentences.zh: 就那样站在路旁的田野里，抬头望着天空，

sentences.zh: 我们当时一定显得非常愚蠢。

sentences.zh: 还有一次，追随者们被指示在多萝西的后院等待。

sentences.zh: 那是冬天，冷得他们不得不使劲用脚跺着冻土地面

sentences.en: to keep their toes from going numb.
sentences.zh: 来防止脚趾失去知觉。

sentences.en: Again, no extraterrestrials came to save them.
sentences.zh: 同样，没有任何外星人来拯救他们。

sentences.en: Each time the flying saucers failed to show up,
sentences.zh: 每当飞碟没有出现时，

sentences.zh: 五十多年后，莉兹也有了类似的感受。

sentences.zh: 她正处于那些寻求者所经历的最初阶段。

sentences.en: He could have just written nothing or he could have said, I'm a scammer.
sentences.zh: 他本可以什么都不写，或者说，我就是个骗子。

sentences.en: Ha ha.
sentences.zh: 哈哈。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: I, but instead he wrote this long letter that had the tones of a love letter to me
sentences.zh: 然而，他却写了这封长信，里面既有写给我的情书的语调，

sentences.en: and the tones of someone who really cared about me.
sentences.zh: 又带有一种真正关心我的人的口吻。

sentences.en: It really is a very confusing email.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一封让人非常困惑的邮件。

sentences.en: I mean, I read it and I did not know what to make of it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我读了之后根本不知道该作何感想。

sentences.en: And I can only imagine what it must have felt like for you to read it.
sentences.zh: 我完全可以想象你读到它时的感受。

sentences.en: What goes through your head at that point, Liz?
sentences.zh: 莉兹，那一刻你脑子里在想什么？

sentences.en: I hate to say this, but it's really a confusing mixture of connection and hatred and disbelief.
sentences.zh: 我很不想这么说，但那真是一种由依恋、恨意和难以置信交织成的复杂心情。

sentences.en: Just a mix of what just happened, what is happening, am I dreaming?
sentences.zh: 脑子里一片混乱：刚刚发生了什么？正在发生什么？我是在做梦吗？

sentences.en: Liz sat in her car for a few hours.
sentences.zh: 莉兹在车里坐了几个小时。

sentences.en: She tried to collect herself.
sentences.zh: 她试图让自己平静下来。

sentences.en: Then, instead of heading to the romantic retreat in Sedona, she drove home.
sentences.zh: 然后，她没有去塞多纳的浪漫度假胜地，而是开车回了家。

sentences.en: As the desert passed by, she slowly let the truth about the last few months of her life sink in.
sentences.zh: 随着窗外的沙漠不断倒退，她慢慢接受了自己过去几个月生活真相的打击。

sentences.en: It was devastating.
sentences.zh: 这太毁灭性了。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm still at a loss as to what to say.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我到现在都不知道该说些什么。

sentences.en: I actually didn't eat for five days.
sentences.zh: 我实际上有五天没有吃东西。

sentences.en: I made myself drink water.
sentences.zh: 我强迫自己喝水。

sentences.en: I could not stomach food.
sentences.zh: 我一点也吃不下东西。

sentences.en: I was just in shock.
sentences.zh: 我当时完全处于震惊之中。

sentences.en: I went to work, but I was useless.
sentences.zh: 我去上班了，但我什么也做不了。

sentences.en: I cried.
sentences.zh: 我哭了。

sentences.en: You know, I called FBI again, and I made a police report.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我又给联邦调查局打了电话，并去警察局报了案。

sentences.en: Nothing made a difference.
sentences.zh: 什么都改变不了。

sentences.en: I didn't know who to talk to.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该跟谁倾诉。

sentences.en: I didn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该做什么。

sentences.en: What was the next step?
sentences.zh: 下一步该怎么走？

sentences.en: How do I gain myself
sentences.zh: 我该如何找回

sentences.en: back?
sentences.zh: 自我？

sentences.en: She started by calling her friends and confessing what had happened.
sentences.zh: 她首先给朋友们打电话，坦白了所发生的一切。

sentences.en: She was so distraught
sentences.zh: 她当时心力交瘁，

sentences.en: and just barely able to get her words out,
sentences.zh: 几乎说不出话来，

sentences.en: just sucking in air and hardly being able to breathe.
sentences.zh: 大口喘着粗气，几乎无法呼吸。

sentences.en: I was so worried about her.
sentences.zh: 我当时非常担心她。

sentences.en: I just felt like, okay, it's over.
sentences.zh: 我只觉得，好吧，这一切都结束了。

sentences.en: She has realized what is happening to her.
sentences.zh: 她已经意识到自己身上发生了什么。

sentences.en: I just remember feeling like all the air had just gone out of me
sentences.zh: 我只记得当时感觉自己体内的力气全被抽空了，

sentences.en: and I was just in an incredible state of relief
sentences.zh: 心中涌起一种难以置信的轻松感，

sentences.en: and a sense of, okay, now we can start working on her
sentences.zh: 还有一种“好了，现在我们可以开始帮她

sentences.en: getting out of this and recovering from it.
sentences.zh: 走出阴影、恢复正常”的想法。

sentences.en: Liz knew she had to untangle why she had refused
sentences.zh: 莉兹知道，她必须理清自己当初为什么会拒绝

sentences.en: to listen to her friend's concerns.
sentences.zh: 听取朋友们的担忧。

sentences.en: She was filled with searing shame.
sentences.zh: 她内心充满了强烈的羞耻感。

sentences.en: Part of why I wanted to tell my story
sentences.zh: 我想讲述自己的故事，部分原因在于

sentences.en: is that I want to continue working on forgiving myself
sentences.zh: 我想继续努力去原谅自己

sentences.en: because I'm not there yet.
sentences.zh: 因为我还没能真正释怀。

sentences.en: I have worse feelings towards myself than towards him.
sentences.zh: 我对自己的厌恶感，甚至超过了对他的憎恨。

sentences.en: I feel I allowed someone who very possibly didn't need money
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己竟然允许一个很可能并不缺钱的人

sentences.en: to be clever enough and insightful and evil to do what he did.
sentences.zh: 用他的狡猾、洞察力和邪恶做出那种事。

sentences.en: But I have more resentment towards myself because I allowed it to get out of hand.
sentences.zh: 但我对自己的怨恨更深，因为是我任由事态发展到失控的地步。

sentences.en: The pain Liz experienced as she confronted the truth
sentences.zh: 莉兹在直面真相时经历的痛苦

sentences.en: helps explain why many people who believe deeply in comforting fictions
sentences.zh: 有助于解释为什么许多深信慰藉性谎言的人

sentences.en: never find their way back to reality.
sentences.zh: 再也无法找到返回现实的路。

sentences.en: Dorothy Martin, Charles Lawhead, and many of the other seekers
sentences.zh: 多萝西·马丁、查尔斯·劳黑德以及许多其他追随者

sentences.en: never surrender their belief in the guardians.
sentences.zh: 始终没有放弃对守护者的信仰。

sentences.en: Each time the flying saucers fail to show up,
sentences.zh: 每当飞碟没有出现时

sentences.en: they quell their dissonance by coming up with new ways to defend their delusions.
sentences.zh: 他们就会通过想出新的方法来捍卫自己的错觉，从而平息内心的认知失调。

sentences.en: Long after the chaotic Christmas caroling scene, Dorothy Martin continued to receive what she said were messages from the guardians.
sentences.zh: 在那个混乱的圣诞颂歌场景过去很久之后，多萝西·马丁仍然不断收到她所说的来自守护者的信息。

sentences.en: She would send these messages to her followers by mail.
sentences.zh: 她会通过邮件将这些信息发送给她的追随者。

sentences.en: Charles Lawhead sold his home in Michigan and decided to travel the country, lecturing about his beliefs.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·劳黑德卖掉了他在密歇根州的家，决定在全国各地旅行，宣讲他的信仰。

sentences.en: One of the researchers who had infiltrated the group reported that he seemed highly confident that everything was still going according to plan.
sentences.zh: 一名潜入该团体的研究人员报告说，他似乎非常自信，认为一切仍然在按计划进行。

sentences.en: In May 1955, Charles Lawhead returned to Michigan.
sentences.zh: 1955年5月，查尔斯·劳黑德回到了密歇根州。

sentences.en: He had received word from a fellow believer that it was time.
sentences.zh: 他接到了一位同道信徒的消息，说时机已到。

sentences.en: At long last, all his sacrifices were going to be repaid.
sentences.zh: 他所有的牺牲终于要得到回报了。

sentences.en: He was going to be picked up by flying saucers.
sentences.zh: 他即将被飞碟接走。

sentences.en: He was instructed to wait on the garage ramp of the largest hotel in the town where he had lived.
sentences.zh: 他被指示在他曾居住过的镇上最大的酒店的车库坡道上等待。

sentences.en: All night long, Charles Lawhead, his wife, his daughter, and another follower
sentences.zh: 整整一夜，查尔斯·劳黑德、他的妻子、他的女儿和另一名追随者

sentences.en: waited on the ramp, gazing up at the heavens.
sentences.zh: 都守在坡道上，仰望苍穹。

sentences.en: As Leon Festinger and his colleagues wrote in their book about the seekers,
sentences.zh: 正如莱昂·费斯廷格和他的同事在他们关于追随者的书中写道的那样

sentences.en: their faith was boundless and their resistance to disconfirmation sublime.
sentences.zh: 他们的信仰坚定不移，对事实否认的抵抗力无与伦比。

sentences.zh: 我是《隐藏的大脑》执行主编。

sentences.zh: 他们是曾与莱昂·费斯廷格共事过的一对研究人员。

sentences.zh: 我们在研究这期节目时联系了埃利奥特和卡罗尔

sentences.zh: 他们就大学档案馆提出了宝贵的建议

sentences.zh: 那里可能存有关于莱昂·费斯廷格工作的资料。

sentences.zh: 埃利奥特和卡罗尔还是一本非常优秀的书的作者

sentences.en: that explores the science of cognitive dissonance.
sentences.zh: 该书探讨了认知失调的科学原理。

sentences.en: It's called Mistakes Were Made, But Not By Me.
sentences.zh: 书名为《错误难免，但我没犯错》。

sentences.en: Thank you, Elliot and Carol.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们，埃利奥特和卡罗尔。

sentences.zh: 我们一直在为未来的《隐藏的大脑》节目寻找

sentences.zh: 精彩的个人故事。

sentences.zh: 如果你有一个关于人生中深刻体验的故事

sentences.zh: 尤其是那种留给你更多疑问而非答案的故事

sentences.zh: 请用手机录下一段简短的语音备忘录

sentences.zh: 将其发送至我们的邮箱 ideas 加上 hiddenbrain.org
